en: Semetey raged
And then berated Kulchoro.
Furious and surging with wrath,
Without caring that the people stood there,
He scolded Kulchoro:
"You are a ruinous boy!
When will you seek the ford?
Whenever you find a bedraggled maiden,
You linger and play with her!
If you carry on this way, you wretch,
You will bring disaster upon me!
You are a calamitous boy;
Beside a maiden before you,
You stretch yourself out and lie there.
If you carry on this way, you wretch,
You will bring disaster upon me!
Whenever there are maidens riding a swing,
You stay to frolic and play;
Whenever there are maidens digging dye,
You play with them improperly!
If you continue like this, little brat,
You will bring disaster upon me!
Whenever there are maidens gathering reeds,
You stay there playing eagerly;
Whenever there are maidens gathering dung,
You stay there playing foolishly!
If you encounter a caravan maiden,
Without saying, 'My elder brother will grieve,'
You remain there playing senselessly.
If you do not abandon this conduct,
You will bring disaster upon me!
When you mount Buurul, you dash away
And vanish in a frenzy;
Without once turning to think,
'My elder brother, my champion, was left behind,'
You forget him entirely!
You beg deceitfully for a horse to ride
And then begin
An uproar beyond all restraint!
Upon a bare and windswept ridge,
You leave me looming like a frozen camel
And ride away!
When you see a maiden, you whine,
And follow alongside her;
You forget your elder brother, great as a mountain,
In the barren steppe,
And deceive him and leave!
You do not ride your own horse;
You doomed wretch,
You never go about speaking the truth!
You are a calamitous boy;
You begin excessive suffering
And trample your elder brother like a traveler
In the empty steppe!
You ought to think, Choro;
Abandon this conduct, Choro.
There are many dark, rugged mountains,
And many enemies who may clash with us;
There are many treacherous passes,
And many warriors with whom blood will be spilled.
How many enemies are there to grapple with?
Behind us, watching and stalking,
Is Kalcha, who slaughtered your father.
He has equipment and ammunition;
Near us,
In China, stands a rogue named Muradyl,
An enemy gathered for mutual destruction.
You begin a terrible uproar;
You deceive me and take my horse,
Then leave me standing like a stump!
You do not understand your own circumstances,
Nor do you travel upon your own road!"
As your lord advanced in a surge of power,
Your poor sister-in-law Churok
Stepped apart from the maidens.
Her mail shirt gleamed;
Radiant, she walked out
Before your hero.
At the sight of her, his body melted,
And your lord's heart was overwhelmed.
The moonlike face
Of Churok, the daughter of Akun, appeared.
Waist like a sheath and face like the moon,
That renowned and doomed beauty
Wore a golden cap upon her head.
That renowned and doomed beauty,
The wretched daughter of Akun,
Displayed her snow-white throat
And overwhelmed the lion's heart.
She stretched with the grace of a lynx,
As though reluctant to spend words in speech.
Her blue leather boots, stitched in paired patterns,
Her double-soled boots,
Gleamed upon her feet.
She walked forward, sleek and stately;
When she laughed, her teeth shone broad as shovels.
Aichurok smiled,
Her face clear as a mirror;
Supple as dressed leather,
She walked smiling and graceful
And came out to welcome her lord.
Whimpering like a puppy,
The heroic lord, the lion—
These were the words Churok spoke;
This is what she said:
"Your words came out in anger.
You have arrived safe and sound.
Your Argyn and Kyrgyz people,
Your elders who have grown old—
I ask after them with longing:
Are the people safe,
And is your aged lion of an elder brother well?
Your land of Keng-Kol, rich with oleaster,
Does it remain safe and prosperous,
And your fortunate Kyrgyz people with it?
Are the possessions inherited from your father
Still safe and sound?
If they are safe, my sovereign,
When will your laughter return?
What shall I do, my sea-like sultan?
I spoke on every side,
Yet you have utterly devoured us with words.
You said, 'They gathered dung.'
Sea-like lord and lion,
Can a bridegroom be like you,
Assailing us from this side?
Lion-like lord,
You displayed your gray-maned fierceness;
Calling us 'maidens gathering reeds,'
You struck us cruelly with false words!
On arriving, you poured out chilling speech;
You called us 'maidens riding a swing.'
Wrapping us in words of torment,
You assailed us from this side!
Do not surge like a cuckoo;
Do not scold Kulchoro!
Do not let your scalp contract in anger;
This conduct of yours is coarse.
Do not quarrel with your servant!
The younger brother you came berating
Has every fortune in balance.
He is a champion upheld by holy spirits!
His right shoulder is broad;
He is a hero who will shatter the Oirot!
At the end of his spine,
He lacks only the breadth of two fingers.
Were it not for that,
His courage would exceed your own
By the length of a spear!
Among all the sons born of humankind,
In what way is he lacking?
He is a hero who dons
Bright-red crimson garments;
If your eyes should turn askance,
He is a hero capable of taking
What stands here before you!
Surging and puffing in fury
At someone you have never met—
This scolding of your younger brother
Is a shameful deed.
For a boy born like this,
Let any bloodthirsty lord be a sacrifice!
Many of his deeds remain unfinished.
Among us too are many boys of twelve
Who cannot manage to walk outside
Or put on their clothes properly.
Even now those boys
Feel no shame before their mothers.
Do not grieve and rage,
Saying, 'I was left in the steppe.'
By joining the boy in your reproach,
Your words have struck us as well!"
After she had spoken in this way,
Semetey stood and said:
"Joined when we were no larger than lice,
United when we were the size of a thumb,
Betrothed when we were tiny as ticks,
When the black cliffs were daubed red,
When infidel and Muslim
Came spreading across the land,
They named us and joined us.
Ninety animals were slaughtered for the feast,
And the people gathered for the wedding.
Ah, my wife Aichurok,
Our marriage was ordained long ago!
Your beauty has long been tested before the people;
My sultan-father, Khan Manas,
Was the matchmaker who found you for me.
When I set out from broad Talas,
Driving fourteen well-fed horses,
I heard your fame from far away
And came expressly in search of you.
You are the dear woman blessed by Khizr!"
When he saw the maiden Churok,
He began speaking delightful words.
Your magnanimous lord's fierce desire
Nearly killed him outright.
When he saw Aichurok,
Lion-born Semetey
Lost all sense of time;
His two eyes became four.
He seized her roughly by the neck,
Wishing to take one kiss from her lips;
Semetey's two eyes became four.
Your noble and magnanimous lord
Immediately dismounted from his horse.
In his handsome mottled coat,
Striding briskly along the road,
He took Churok, the daughter of Akun,
By her slender forearm,
And placed his hand upon her breast.
His eyes fixed upon her like an argali's;
He drifted away in rapture.
Your gray-maned lord panted,
And, about to press himself upon Churok,
Nearly died where he stood.
Seeing her lord's condition,
The beautiful Aichurok below him
Darkened Allah's sun in the sky,
